packageRules.description: Gradle updates land on the dependency dashboard instead of opening PRs on their own, for two reasons that both go away at cutover. (1) Until then this repository is a COPY of modules that still build and publish from compose-ai-tools; its CI checks the device-dimensions catalog against a compose-ai-tools checkout, and its publishing is hard-blocked (see docs/VERSIONING.md). Letting the toolchain drift independently creates divergence that has to be reconciled by hand later, for no benefit while nothing here ships. (2) gradle/libs.versions.toml came across whole: 174 entries, of which the nine modules here reference about 13. Renovate reads the catalog, not the build files, so unattended it would open PRs for ~160 dependencies this repository does not consume. Prune the catalog and finish the cutover, then delete this rule — the guards below are written to still apply.

Never take a `…-compat` backport artifact. JetBrains publishes compatibility variants of the kotlinx libraries under a `<version>-<oldline>.x-compat` suffix (e.g. `kotlinx-datetime:0.8.0-0.6.x-compat`, the 0.8.0 code recompiled against the 0.6.x API) and Renovate's gradle versioning ranks that suffix ABOVE the plain release, so it proposes a downgrade of API surface dressed as an upgrade (compose-ai-tools#3359). Filtering the suffix out of the candidate list — rather than disabling the update — keeps Renovate offering the next genuine release.

robolectric: released versions only. Robolectric publishes a rolling `4.17-SNAPSHOT` to Sonatype and Renovate ranks it above `4.17-beta-2`, but this build declares no snapshot repository (nor should it, for a reproducible build) — so the bump resolves nowhere and fails every Android configuration. Betas and RCs are still fair game; only `-SNAPSHOT` is excluded. gradle/libs.versions.toml cites this rule by name.
